sophia: Heads-up — noticed a weird telemetry spike after enabling preview snapshots for a config rollout this morning. Dashboard showed duplicated "events.change_applied" counts for ~40m. Anyone seen this before? :thinking:

matt: Hmm, saw something similar last quarter but that was tied to the dry-run reconciliation job replaying events. Did you have dry-run + audit replay enabled?

sophia: No replay. We had preview-snapshot=on and sampling=0.1 for the rollout. The spike aligns with the snapshot window at 09:02.

eva: Can you paste the raw event payloads (redact ids) if you have them? Quick check: are we double-instrumenting both the console and the router for the same config-change id?

sophia: Pasted minimal example below — removed user ids:
messages: sophia: Heads-up — noticed a weird telemetry spike after enabling preview snapshots for a config rollout this morning. Dashboard showed duplicated "events.change_applied" counts for ~40m. Anyone seen this before? :thinking:
matt: Hmm, saw something similar last quarter but that was tied to the dry-run reconciliation job replaying events. Did you have dry-run + audit replay enabled?
sophia: No replay. We had preview-snapshot=on and sampling=0.1 for the rollout. The spike aligns with the snapshot window at 09:02.
eva: Can you paste the raw event payloads (redact ids) if you have them? Quick check: are we double-instrumenting both the console and the router for the same config-change id?

zach: That source field looks suspicious. We should standardize source -> origin and only emit from the orchestration layer. Console-preview should send a single "preview_request" event and let the orchestrator emit the canonical "change_applied" when it actually applies.
matt: Agreed. Short-term: add a dedupe key on telemetry using config_change_id + origin_type. Long-term: change event contract so only one service is the source-of-truth for change_applied.
sophia: Quick question on dedupe: do we want the dedupe to be a client-side filter (console SDK) or a server-side dedupe at the telemetry pipeline? Server-side easier to roll out but adds delay.

eva: Server-side IMO. We already have a streaming dedupe step in the metrics ingestor (kafka consumer). Add a small 1hr sliding window for config_change_id. That would handle both duplicate emits and short replays.

zach: One caveat — if we dedupe purely by config_change_id we might mask legitimate re-apply attempts (manual rollback/restore cycles). Can we include a fingerprint: config_change_id + commit_sha + action_type?

sophia: Good point. commit_sha present on these events? I can add it to console payloads.

Also, can we tweak the dashboard to expose a new metric: "slo_burn_by_change" that correlates change_id to error/latency percentiles so on spikes we can quickly tell if the change did harm.

matt: +1 for the slo_burn_by_change metric. Implementation idea: during rollout, push a temporary tag (config_change_id) into request traces and have the metrics job join traces -> rolling SLO windows. Might be heavy but very actionable.

eva: For rollout UX: console should show a small "telemetry health" badge for preview snapshots: green/yellow/red based on event coverage and dedupe rate. That will help SOC/PMs know if the telemetry is reliable before promoting.

sophia: Next steps I can take today:
- add commit_sha to console preview payloads
- file a short ticket to add server-side dedupe in metrics ingestor (1hr sliding window)
- prototype a slo_burn_by_change query in the metrics notebook (basic join on trace tags)

Would any of you like to pair on the dedupe patch?
zach: I can pair tomorrow for 30m — can help with the sliding window logic and ensure we don't inflate cardinality.
matt: I can take the console change to send commit_sha and origin_type.
deploy-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance on metrics-ingestor at 02:00 UTC tomorrow. Will briefly restart consumer groups. :wrench:
sophia: Thanks — we'll avoid deploying the dedupe patch during that window. I'll create the ticket and link planned PRs. :thumbsup:
